purpose: Curated current primary-source records that must be merged into the relevant Mission Timers before scoring and publication. Records distinguish enacted law, active enforcement, measured conditions, implementation, counter-signals and bounded hypothesis.

records.title: Australia's under-16 social-media account restriction is in force
records.summary: From 10 December 2025, age-restricted social-media platforms must take reasonable steps to prevent Australians under 16 from creating or keeping accounts. The regulator reports continuing compliance monitoring.
records.evidenceLevel: Official regulator · law in force · active compliance
records.identityLink: Platforms must operate age-assurance systems, while privacy restrictions and platform responsibility remain part of the legal design.
records.claimBoundary: This proves mandatory age restriction and age-assurance deployment in Australia. It does not prove that the stated child-safety purpose is a covert digital-ID plan.

records.title: Australia updates the platform definition used by its social-media minimum-age law
records.summary: Australia updated the rules in March 2026 to focus the minimum-age obligation on account-based recommender systems and design features such as endless feeds, feedback signals and time-limited content.
records.identityLink: The regulated scope determines where platforms must deploy account-age controls.
records.claimBoundary: The update demonstrates continuing implementation, not a finding about hidden motive.

records.title: UK age checks are deployed at unprecedented scale under the Online Safety Act
records.summary: Ofcom's July 2026 statutory report states that many services are required to use highly effective age assurance and that age checks have been deployed at unprecedented scale.
records.evidenceLevel: Official regulator · statutory report · active enforcement
records.identityLink: Regulated services must determine whether users meet age thresholds using highly effective age assurance.
records.claimBoundary: This proves large-scale age assurance. It does not establish that every service must collect a government identity document or that a single universal identity database exists.

records.title: EU urges Member States to make a common age-verification app available by the end of 2026
records.summary: The European Commission adopted a recommendation on 29 April 2026 urging Member States to accelerate rollout of the EU age-verification app. The app may operate independently or be integrated into a European Digital Identity Wallet.
records.identityLink: The Commission explicitly permits integration with European Digital Identity Wallet infrastructure.
records.claimBoundary: Wallet compatibility is documented infrastructure convergence. It does not prove that child safety is merely a cover or that the wallet will become compulsory for all online activity.

records.title: EU age-verification blueprint is technically ready and supports national eIDs, passports and identity cards
records.summary: The Commission says its age-verification solution became feature-ready in April 2026. Proof of age can be issued from national eIDs, passports, identity cards, banking apps or offline activation, while the design aims to disclose only the required age threshold.
records.identityLink: The proof can be bootstrapped from government identity documents, national eIDs or trusted applications, while using selective disclosure and zero-knowledge techniques.
records.claimBoundary: The identity-document onboarding route is documented. The privacy-preserving design is also documented and must be included as counter-evidence against claims of inevitable centralised identity tracking.

records.title: Denmark, France, Greece, Italy and Spain are adopting customised versions of the EU age-verification solution
records.summary: The Commission identifies five Member States taking up the common technical solution with a view to publishing customised national age-verification applications.
records.evidenceLevel: Official EU rollout record · multi-jurisdiction adoption
records.identityLink: The national apps use a harmonised proof-of-age architecture designed to interoperate with European identity-wallet standards.
records.claimBoundary: Common architecture across several countries proves policy and technical convergence, not a secret unified identity mandate.

records.title: France enacted a digital-majority framework requiring parental consent below 15 and technical verification
records.summary: France's digital-majority law requires social-network providers to refuse registration by children under 15 without parental consent and provides for certified technical solutions to verify age and parental authorisation, subject to implementation and European-law constraints.
records.identityLink: The law expressly requires technical age and parental-authorisation verification mechanisms.
records.claimBoundary: The statute is real, but practical enforcement and compatibility with EU law must be tracked separately from the enacted text.

records.title: EU protection-of-minors guidelines and age-verification prototype establish a common DSA implementation route
records.summary: The European Commission issued protection-of-minors guidelines and an age-verification prototype under the Digital Services Act, creating a common compliance and technical route for platforms operating across the EU.
records.evidenceLevel: Official EU regulatory guidance · technical prototype
records.identityLink: The common prototype provides reusable proof-of-age infrastructure for platform compliance.
records.claimBoundary: The DSA route establishes common compliance expectations but the guidelines themselves do not prove a universal compulsory identity system.

records.title: Every EU Member State must make at least one European Digital Identity Wallet available by the end of 2026
records.summary: The European Commission says Member States will make wallets available to citizens, residents and businesses by the end of 2026. More than 550 companies and public authorities across 26 Member States and associated countries have participated in large-scale pilots.
records.evidenceLevel: Official EU implementation page · statutory rollout
records.identityLink: The wallet is designed for public and private services using common standards and interoperable person-identification data.
records.claimBoundary: Mandatory state provision and common standards are documented. Official policy says individual use is voluntary and selective disclosure is a core safeguard.

records.title: EU remote-onboarding standards for digital identity wallets entered implementing law in April 2026
records.summary: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/798 sets reference standards and specifications for remote onboarding to European Digital Identity Wallets at high assurance levels.
records.identityLink: The regulation operationalises identity-wallet onboarding rather than leaving it at policy or pilot stage.
records.claimBoundary: This proves technical and legal implementation. It does not prove that all services will require the wallet.

records.title: European Media Freedom Act platform safeguards move into implementation
records.summary: Commission guidelines published in February 2026 require very large online platforms to notify qualifying media providers before removing professional journalistic content and explain the reasons, with a response window before removal.
records.evidenceLevel: Official EU implementation guidelines · binding legislative framework
records.identityLink: The framework formalises how platforms classify media providers and control removal procedures.
records.claimBoundary: The rules show platform power is being legally structured and constrained; they do not establish that all moderation is state censorship.

records.title: Council of Europe endorses an updated Rule of Law Checklist covering emergency powers, digital technologies and private actors exercising public power
records.summary: The updated checklist was endorsed in May 2026. It requires emergency measures to be necessary, proportionate, temporary and subject to parliamentary and judicial control, and extends rule-of-law expectations to dominant private actors or companies performing public tasks.
records.evidenceLevel: Official Council of Europe standard · endorsed governance benchmark
records.identityLink: The standard directly addresses emergency powers, public-sector technology, surveillance and private providers whose decisions have public impact.
records.claimBoundary: This is a current benchmark and warning framework, not proof that every country is presently abusing emergency powers.

records.title: Euro area inflation was 2.8% in June 2026 while energy prices were 8.7% higher than a year earlier
records.summary: Eurostat reported euro-area annual inflation of 2.8% in June 2026, with energy making the largest component increase at 8.7%. EU annual inflation was 2.9%.
records.identityLink: Energy and service-price pressure directly affects household survival and small-business operating costs.
records.claimBoundary: The data measure price pressure; they do not establish a coordinated intention to make households poorer.

records.title: Household real income per person barely increased in the latest EU quarterly accounts
records.summary: Eurostat reported that euro-area household real income per capita increased by 0.1% in the fourth quarter of 2025 while real consumption increased by 0.5%.
records.identityLink: Weak real-income growth limits household capacity to absorb continued housing, energy and food costs.
records.claimBoundary: The data show limited income growth, not inevitable household collapse.

records.title: EU house prices continued rising in the first quarter of 2026
records.summary: Eurostat reported annual house-price increases of 4.7% in the euro area and 5.1% in the EU in the first quarter of 2026.
records.identityLink: Price growth affects affordability, mortgage access and household leverage.
records.claimBoundary: Rising prices demonstrate affordability pressure but do not alone prove ownership concentration or deliberate exclusion.

records.title: Euro-area banks tightened standards for housing loans and consumer credit in the second quarter of 2026
records.summary: The ECB's July 2026 bank lending survey found moderate tightening for firms and net tightening for housing loans and consumer credit, with banks expecting further tightening across categories.
records.identityLink: Tighter approval criteria and rising rejection shares affect housing access, household credit and business refinancing.
records.claimBoundary: The survey records bank behaviour and expectations; it does not prove a planned credit shutdown.

records.title: ECB says cash acceptance declined from 96% to 88% between 2021 and 2024 while supporting legal protection for cash
records.summary: The ECB reported declining company acceptance of cash and supports EU legislation strengthening cash access and legal-tender acceptance, including concern about no-cash policies.
records.evidenceLevel: Official central-bank statement · measured acceptance trend
records.identityLink: The record shows both erosion in practical cash acceptance and an active institutional countermeasure to protect payment choice.
records.claimBoundary: Declining acceptance is real, but the ECB's stated policy is to preserve cash rather than abolish it.

records.title: Digital euro rulebook entered a new draft stage in July 2026 with a 2027 pilot and possible first issuance in 2029
records.summary: The ECB published draft rulebook version 0.91 in July 2026. It says the digital euro would be distributed through banks, work online and offline, and could be ready for potential issuance in 2029 if legislation is adopted in 2026.
records.evidenceLevel: Official central-bank project update · rulebook and pilot preparation
records.identityLink: Banks and payment intermediaries would distribute a common public digital-payment instrument with mandatory-acceptance provisions proposed in legislation.
records.claimBoundary: Development is advanced, but issuance has not been decided and official design says cash remains available and offline privacy is protected.

records.title: European Ombudsman publishes 2025 annual accountability and transparency report
records.summary: The European Ombudsman published its annual report in April 2026, framing transparency, accountability, citizen rights and meaningful engagement as central safeguards amid declining public trust.
records.identityLink: The report provides a current oversight route for maladministration, access, transparency and institutional accountability.
records.claimBoundary: The report establishes ongoing transparency challenges and oversight activity, not that all missing records are deliberate concealment.

records.title: 2026 EU Rule of Law Report assesses justice, corruption, media pluralism and checks and balances across 31 countries
records.summary: The Commission's seventh annual report, published 17 July 2026, records reforms and continuing challenges across justice systems, anti-corruption frameworks, media freedom and institutional checks and balances.
records.jurisdiction: European Union; Albania; Montenegro; North Macedonia; Serbia
records.identityLink: The report is the current cross-country evidence base for institutional accountability, media concentration, judicial independence and checks and balances.
records.claimBoundary: The report shows uneven progress and risks; it does not support a single undifferentiated score for every country.

records.title: Stronger EU-wide anti-corruption rules took effect in June 2026
records.summary: The new directive harmonises corruption offences, minimum penalties, investigation tools, limitation periods and preventive obligations for public officials, individuals and companies.
records.evidenceLevel: Official EU law · rules in force
records.identityLink: The directive expands the common legal framework governing public power, influence trading and corporate liability.
records.claimBoundary: Stronger law is a counter-signal; practical enforcement and deterrence must still be measured.

records.title: ENTSO-E's Summer Outlook finds no systemic European electricity adequacy risk but identifies specific weak regions
records.summary: The May 2026 assessment found no systemic adequacy risk for most of Europe, while identifying structural or specific risks in Moldova, Ireland, Malta and Cyprus and emphasising the need for flexibility, interconnection and storage.
records.identityLink: The report identifies current vulnerabilities while providing a strong counter-signal against claims of imminent continent-wide grid failure.
records.claimBoundary: Regional risks exist, but the official assessment does not support a present systemic European blackout claim.

records.title: ENISA reports improving cybersecurity maturity across EU critical sectors under NIS2
records.summary: The May 2026 NIS360 assessment found improved cybersecurity maturity while sector criticality remained high, reflecting active NIS2 implementation and continuing infrastructure exposure.
records.identityLink: The record measures both resilience gains and continuing dependence on highly critical connected systems.
records.claimBoundary: Improving maturity lowers immediate pressure but does not remove concentrated infrastructure risk.

records.title: EMA continues publishing active critical medicine shortage communications in 2026
records.summary: EMA's 2026 shortage communications include human insulin, ifosfamide, cyclophosphamide and other medicines, with updated mitigation recommendations and monitoring through the shortages network.
records.evidenceLevel: Official medicines regulator · active shortage communications
records.identityLink: The current list shows real access pressure alongside an active regulatory mitigation system.
records.claimBoundary: Specific shortages are documented; they do not establish universal healthcare collapse.

records.title: EEA says renewables reduce energy prices and vulnerability to fossil-fuel supply shocks
records.summary: A July 2026 EEA assessment identifies homegrown renewable electricity as a primary route to reducing exposure to volatile imported fossil fuels and rising energy prices.
records.identityLink: The assessment is a counter-signal showing that domestic generation and storage can reduce affordability and supply pressure.
records.claimBoundary: Renewable deployment can improve resilience, but grid, storage and investment constraints remain.

records.title: EEA reports growing European climate-resilience pressure from drought, floods and extreme weather
records.summary: The EEA's June 2026 resilience update highlights severe drought, flooding, wildfires and record temperatures, with uneven adaptation and direct consequences for water, agriculture, infrastructure and public health.
records.identityLink: The record links water availability and extreme-weather impacts to food production and essential-service resilience.
records.claimBoundary: Climate and water risks are documented; local severity and adaptation capacity vary materially by region.

records.title: UNCTAD reports record trade growth alongside shipping, energy and logistics price pressure
records.summary: UNCTAD's July/August 2026 update estimates strong first-half trade growth but says a significant share reflects higher prices, with Strait of Hormuz disruptions raising energy, transport, logistics and production costs.
records.identityLink: The report links geopolitical chokepoints to freight, fertilizer, energy and production costs across essential supply chains.
records.claimBoundary: Trade is still expanding, which is a counter-signal against a present global supply-chain collapse.

records.title: EU launches a mechanism to aggregate critical-raw-material demand and connect buyers, suppliers, finance and storage
records.summary: The April 2026 Raw Materials Mechanism aims to reduce concentrated third-country dependencies by aggregating industry demand and connecting companies with alternative suppliers, financiers and storage providers.
records.identityLink: The mechanism is a documented public-private coordination layer for strategic industrial inputs.
records.claimBoundary: Public-private coordination is real; this source does not show covert ownership or unlawful market control.

records.title: European Democracy Shield implementation covers information-space integrity, political safety and AI in elections
records.summary: The Commission's democracy programme includes situational awareness, response capacity, political safety, AI in electoral processes and anti-SLAPP measures, supported by the European cooperation network on elections.
records.evidenceLevel: Official EU democracy and electoral-integrity programme
records.identityLink: The programme formalises cross-border monitoring of information manipulation, electoral technology and political threats.
records.claimBoundary: Protective coordination can strengthen integrity but also requires transparency and safeguards against political misuse.

records.title: ILO finds real but uneven GenAI productivity effects and limited evidence of large-scale displacement so far
records.summary: The ILO's June 2026 review finds real but uneven productivity gains, limited large-scale job displacement to date, and rising risks around inequality, younger-worker opportunities, autonomy and job quality.
records.identityLink: The evidence supports a transformation and inequality clock more strongly than an immediate mass-unemployment claim.
records.claimBoundary: Exposure and task change do not equal confirmed job loss; large-scale displacement remains limited in the reviewed evidence.

records.title: OECD says AI is changing skill demand and can displace jobs if transitions are poorly managed
records.summary: The July 2026 OECD paper describes AI as a general-purpose technology changing labour markets and skill requirements, with displacement risk depending on sector, place, skill level and policy response.
records.identityLink: The current pressure is concentrated in task and skill transition rather than a uniform employment collapse.
records.claimBoundary: The report identifies displacement risk, not a fixed number of inevitable job losses.

records.title: 2026 Rule of Law Report says media-market concentration and editorial independence concerns persist
records.summary: The Commission reports ongoing EMFA implementation and continuing concerns over media-market concentration, public-service-media independence, journalist safety and state-advertising transparency.
records.identityLink: The report provides current official evidence that ownership and editorial-independence risks remain material despite new legal safeguards.
records.claimBoundary: Risk varies by country and market; the report does not establish one unified controller of European media.

records.title: IMF projects global public debt reaching 100% of GDP by 2029 amid rising interest and geopolitical risks
records.summary: The April 2026 Fiscal Monitor says global public debt rose to just under 94% of GDP in 2025 and is projected to reach 100% by 2029, with interest burdens and sovereign-market structure increasing vulnerability.
records.identityLink: The report documents macro-level debt vulnerability and repricing risk rather than a specific imminent banking failure.
records.claimBoundary: High aggregate debt is not the same as universal sovereign insolvency.

records.title: ECB says euro-area financial vulnerabilities remain elevated under geopolitical and energy-supply stress
records.summary: The May 2026 Financial Stability Review identifies market, non-bank, bank funding, credit and debt-service risks arising from geopolitical and energy shocks.
records.identityLink: The review connects energy and trade shocks to debt servicing, bank credit, liquidity and non-bank amplification channels.
records.claimBoundary: Vulnerabilities are elevated, but the review does not forecast inevitable systemic failure.

records.title: European Commission study identifies climate, demographic and regulatory pressure on farm income and viability
records.summary: A May 2026 Commission study based on fifteen cases across eleven Member States examines how climate pressure, demographic change and regulation affect farm income, resilience and long-term viability.
records.identityLink: The evidence links water, input, regulatory and demographic pressures to domestic production capacity and farm survival.
records.claimBoundary: The study documents pressure and adaptation pathways; it does not establish a deliberate policy to eliminate independent farmers.
